body:
# Independent audit of exponential erosion and active-cap bulge payment

Audited `candidate 1357de39d4196ea9`
in full. Result: PASS. No mathematical correction is required. I also
independently recomputed the interval moments and all moving-event
formulas symbolically. The exact verifier passes with

    work/math-venv/bin/python supporting computation verify_exponential_erosion_active_bulge.py

The ordinary system Python lacks SymPy; the workspace math environment
contains it. This is a runtime dependency only, not a certificate issue.

## 1. Real-base convexity and preservation of positive integer fibers

The convexity proof is valid on the entire real base, rather than merely
at sampled indices. If two fibers contain balls centered at x_0,x_1
with radii r(z_0),r(z_1), convexity of E contains their interpolated
ball with interpolated radius. A convex nonnegative radius at the
intermediate base is no larger, so its smaller ball is also contained.
The exponential is finite, continuous, positive, and convex, making
the corrected set closed as well as convex. The zero continuous-normal
factor in a vertical source inequality is correctly zero.

On a compact set of (h,v) parameters, all radii are O(delta). Each
original A_z has a positive inradius, and it is contained in the
enlarged fiber. Finitely many such fibers therefore have a common
positive surviving inradius for all sufficiently small delta. No
positive fiber disappears. No uniform inradius at EVERY real base
is asserted or needed. Erosion cannot create additional positive
integer fibers. The canonical hull of all corrected positive fibers
has exactly those traces by convexity, and the existing one-sided
thickening applies when its base affine span is deficient.

## 2. Division by the loss scale, differentiability, and invertibility

The raw parameter derivative at zero removal would indeed be singular.
The note correctly divides lost volume by delta before invoking an
inverse argument. For a convex full-dimensional fiber K and radii a
strictly below its inradius, the inner-parallel loss satisfies

    |K|-|K inner-eroded by a|=integral_0^a S(K inner-eroded by b) db.

Coarea gives the equality; continuity of convex surface area along
these inner bodies makes its derivative S(K inner-eroded by a) at
every such positive a, and gives the right derivative S(K) at zero.
For the enlarging fibers K_t converging to A_z, the inner bodies
converge uniformly to A_z as the small radius varies in any compact
parameter family. Surface areas therefore converge uniformly as well.

With a=delta exp(h+v.d_z), the derivatives of the divided loss are

    partial_h R=exp(h+v.d_z) S(K_t inner-eroded by a),
    partial_v R=d_z partial_h R.

These formulas prove the claimed C1 convergence in (h,v). They require
no differentiability in the external parameter t, including when the
enlarged body changes combinatorial type.

The limiting prescribed mean lies in relint conv(P-j). Its log-partition
objective is coercive on the effective base span: its recession is the
strict positive support gap from that interior point. Its Hessian is
the covariance of strictly positive weights at all P, and hence is
positive definite on the span. The full mass-and-mean Jacobian is
sum weight_z q_z q_z^T, positive definite because the q_z span.
The stated fixed-J contraction follows by first making the parameter
ball small, then the uniform derivative error and target error small.
It maps that ball into itself. This proves EXACT equations (4), not
only matching of first derivatives. Rank zero is covered by the single
mass parameter h and an empty v vector.

The target first moment (kappa,r_t-j), with the second coordinate
unmultiplied by kappa, is correct: the required loss BASE MEAN is
j+(r_t-j)/kappa. The resulting retained mean is precisely j.
Uniformity on compact subsets of the relative interior is valid;
no bounded parameter claim at the boundary is made.

## 3. The interior-base point bulge is an actual construction

For a full-dimensional polytope fiber A_z0 strictly contained in C_z0,
one may choose an interior starting point and an unused endpoint so
their segment exits through a relative facet interior. The excluded
choices hit finitely many faces of codimension at least two. The new
point just beyond that facet remains in C_z0. Its convex hull with
the old facet is an added pyramid of fixed positive base area and
height proportional to t, so the own-fiber added volume is >=c_0 t.
This includes d=1, where the facet has H_0 measure one.

The O(t) TOTAL added volume deserves the finite-inequality argument
given in the note. At each fixed integer base, ignore vertical
inequalities, which have no continuous restriction. If the remaining
old fiber inequalities are u_f.x<=c_f, choose x_z in int A_z and put
eta_z=min_f(c_f-u_f.x_z)>0. All inequalities of the enlarged hull
are bounded by the old ones relaxed by at most B t. If y lies in that
relaxed fiber, then

    x_z+(y-x_z)/(1+B t/eta_z) belongs to A_z.

Thus the relaxed fiber lies in the homothetic expansion
x_z+(1+B t/eta_z)(A_z-x_z), whose volume increase is O(t).
There are only finitely many integer fibers, giving the claimed upper
bound. Base-affine equations remain exact, because the added point
has a base already in P. This argument remains valid when several
ambient facets restrict to the same fiber facet.

A fixed positive fraction of added mass consequently stays at the
interior base z_0. Convexity of conv P carries its fixed relative ball
into a uniform ball about every added-base mean. A single kappa<1
near enough to one makes all dilated loss means remain in a compact
subset of relint conv P. Section 2 therefore really corrects this
bulge with less deleted than added mass. No independent fiber trimming
or convexity inference from moments is hidden in the construction.

## 4. Centroid payment identities and their limits

The signed source identity new=old+addition-removal gives both exact
continuous first moments and equation (12) with the correct signs.
Base-moment cancellation legitimately permits the integer tilt term
inside the influence function. The coarse sufficient cost includes
the full possible removal of OLD mass and the actual continuous
centroid displacement. It does not assume the corrected body contains D.

For the first-order influence law, the plane-null hypotheses on both
limiting added and removed measures are essential and are explicitly
included. They justify passing moving cap indicators through weak
convergence. The nonfacet hypothesis gives differentiability of the
old section-volume profile; unit continuous normal gives coarea
factor one. These facts yield the coefficient -(S_H/m)L and
integral W_H dmu_D=0. The positive included band and far excluded band
have the stated signs. Coincident facets are explicitly excluded from
this differentiable formula and assigned to the exact identity.

## 5. All-real-slope verification of the zero-slack example

The original centered widths (5,9/2,3,1) are concave and have weighted
integer mean zero. The actual upper-endpoint bulge at base 1 remains
concave on the entire real interval for 0<=delta<=1/4. Its lower
boundary is unchanged. The subsequent exponential real-base erosion
is convex by Section 1 and remains inside the designated C.

The four exact lost lengths sum to 15delta/19 and have first base
moment delta, exactly paying the added mass at base 1. All four new
widths stay positive. Independent calculation gives

    m_delta=(8delta+513)/38,
    base first moment=0,
    c_delta=3delta(5delta+19)/(8delta+513).

I reproduced all five consecutive breakpoint differences in (20),
including their positive denominators. The rational bounds prove
strict ordering throughout the CLOSED parameter interval [0,1/4].
The own-fiber cap stays proper throughout. The seven actual slope
values between events are exactly 0,-1,0,2,0,-1,0.

For clarity, the upward profile has only four extreme plateau values:
the two exterior limits, the interior minimum, and the interior maximum.
Their downward complements give exactly the four Q_i in (21).
This exhausts every real slope, including all the flat active slope
families at delta=0. Vertical closed caps include the entire anchor
fiber and dominate the corresponding nonvertical limits. Their possible
positive boundary mass therefore cannot lower the asserted depth.

Each of the four independently computed Q_i-beta m_delta agrees with
(23), and its numerator is strictly positive for 0<delta<=1/4.
Consequently the all-cap improvement follows from finite EXACT moving
events, not an upgrade of fixed-slope derivative tests. For regular
representatives of the four original active slope families, the
influence law also reproduces the derivatives
55/513, 53/1026, 169/513, 395/1026. At the endpoints of those families
the moving-event formulas supply the required one-sided control.

The zero-slack budget is beta=25/54, strictly below gamma_1=1/2.
The note states this explicitly. It proves that this particular active
budget can be paid by a constructive correction, not that the sharp
gamma_d budget of an arbitrary extracted maximizer can be paid.

## 6. Audit of the appended parameter family

The added Section 7 also PASSES. I independently recomputed its exact
mass and centroid, all five moving-event differences, and all four
deficits symbolically in the TWO free variables a and delta. The
formulas (24)--(27) agree. The extended verifier also passes.

At delta=0, the four extreme cap values all equal (7a+4)/4, while
M_a=(7a+6)/2. Thus the exact depth is the asserted beta_a. The upper
boundary slopes remain ordered for every a>=3 and delta<=1/4;
the lower boundary and eroded widths remain valid. All five event
numerators stay positive by the stated endpoint bounds. The anchor
fiber is proper uniformly as well: 0<=c<=delta<=1/4, while
r_0=3a/4-delta/19>1/4 and l_0<0.

The first and fourth deficit numerators are positive after bounding
their negative delta coefficients at 1/4. The second delta-free
quadratic is positive at a=3 and has positive derivative there and
beyond; its delta terms are positive. The third numerator is immediate.
The first-order values in (27) have the stated monotonicity, and their
common lower bound 53/1026 is correct. This is a bound on ABSOLUTE
first-order cap deficits, not on normalized depth gains: the source
mass increases with a. The note correctly avoids taking a paid
deformation limit at one fixed half-depth-maximal body.
